skill.name: convex-expert
skill.description: Convex backend specialist. Use this agent for any code inside a `convex/` directory — function definitions, schemas, indexes, queries, mutations, actions, HTTP endpoints, cron jobs, file storage, auth wiring, and component installation. Knows the object-form function syntax, validator patterns, resource limits, and component ecosystem that generic Claude routinely gets wrong.
skill.summary: Build and review Convex backend code with validated functions, indexed queries, and staged schema changes.
skill.author: convex

security_audit.summary: Seven backtick matches are inline references, and the Convex account check is not host reconnaissance. The verification rule does request CLI execution and a deployment push without requiring approval, with a possible local deployment configuration change. No evidence found of secret collection or an attempt to manipulate the audit.

remediation.issue: Verification can push backend code to an existing deployment without explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Default to local type checking. Ask for explicit approval for the named deployment before pushing any code.

remediation.issue: An unsuccessful account check can trigger anonymous setup, which may change local deployment configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Stop if the account check fails. Explain the possible configuration change and obtain approval before initializing an anonymous deployment.

remediation.issue: The verification commands use npx, which may fetch packages if the tools are not installed.
remediation.suggestion: Use the project's installed and locked TypeScript and Convex tools. Ask before installing any missing packages.

content.value_statement: Convex backend changes can fail when functions, indexes, or schema updates do not follow platform rules. This skill guides assistants through Convex-specific implementation and review.
actual_capabilities: Define Convex functions in object form with argument and return validators.
Match query read paths to schema indexes and bound results with pagination or limits.
Keep server-only functions internal and use generated imports.
Plan schema changes for existing records by adding optional fields before backfilling and enforcing them.
Separate Node runtime actions from queries and mutations.
Recommend Convex components for chat features and multi-step workflows.
limitations: The skill provides instructions and does not include a standalone testing or deployment tool.
Type checking and deployment verification depend on the project's CLI tools and configuration.
Type checking does not prove runtime behavior or access control correctness.
The built-in verification rule can push code to a configured deployment unless you limit the task to local checks.

use_cases.title: Write a First Convex Query
use_cases.description: Use the current schema to define a query with argument and return validators.

use_cases.title: Review Queries on Growing Tables
use_cases.description: Identify unbounded reads and recommend indexes and pagination for the affected query paths.

use_cases.title: Plan a Schema Update for Existing Data
use_cases.description: Break a required field change into an optional field, a backfill, and a final validation step.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Convex Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the Convex schema and explain this query's argument and return validators. Suggest corrections without changing files or running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Validated Mutation
prompt_templates.prompt: Add an internal mutation that updates a task status using the existing schema. Include argument and return validators. Do not push to a deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Indexed Read Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Review how tasks are listed by project and status. Recommend a schema index and bounded pagination. Keep the review local.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Staged Schema Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a migration that makes owner IDs required on existing task records. Describe optional validation, backfill, and final checks. Do not run the migration or deploy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Maintainers planning a change to populated tables

output_examples.input: Review a task list that loads every record before filtering by project.
output: Add a project index to the task table.
Query that index for the requested project and return a page of results.

output_examples.input: Plan how to add a required owner to existing tasks.
output: Add owner as an optional field and define how to determine each task's owner.
Backfill and check existing records before making the field required.

best_practices: Read the current schema and any generated guidelines before editing Convex functions.
Use argument and return validators, and keep functions internal unless a client needs them.
Run local checks first and approve the exact deployment target before any push.
anti_patterns: Collect every row from a growing table before filtering the results.
Make a new field required before backfilling existing records.
Treat a deployment push as a read-only verification step.

faq.question: What code does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Convex backend code, including schemas, indexes, validators, queries, mutations, and actions.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for a review of query bounds, validator coverage, generated imports, or function visibility.

faq.question: Does it support schema changes on populated tables?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends adding an optional field, backfilling records, and then making the field required.

faq.question: Can I use it without deploying?
faq.answer: Yes. Specify a read-only review or local type checking, and explicitly prohibit deployment pushes and configuration changes.

faq.question: Does it include Convex components?
faq.answer: No. It recommends Convex components for chat and multi-step workflows, but does not bundle them.

faq.question: Which assistants are listed as compatible?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Local inspection and verification depend on the tools available to your assistant.
